title: Add latency-cliff detector and adaptive-concurrency rollout guard
author: Miguel Torres
description: Motivation: We've observed hard 'latency cliff' failure modes where p95/p99 jump sharply within a short window even though rolling averages look stable; these events bypass percentile-based canaries and lead to partial outages. This PR implements a latency-cliff detector that detects rapid percentile deltas across short windows and wires an adaptive-concurrency rollout guard that temporarily reduces per-replica concurrency and pauses rollouts when a cliff is detected. Changes include detector algorithm, integration with the canary evaluation pipeline, a lightweight local load harness for reproducible cliffs, dashboards, and unit/integration tests. Checklist: [x] detector algorithm and unit tests, [x] canary integration and gating, [x] adaptive-concurrency policy and actuator, [x] dashboards and runbook, [x] CI flake fixes. Rollout plan: rollout as a guarded feature flag for 2 weeks, enable in perf-canary staging, monitor metrics and KB/alerts, then enable for canary->prod rollouts. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes; the guard is opt-in via canary config; defaults are off. Performance cost: detector is O(1) per incoming metric update and uses bounded memory. Related: ENG-1428, ENG-1534. Test plan: unit tests cover algorithm edge cases; integration test injects synthetic cliff using examples/load-profiles/stepped-cliff.yaml; manual verification with dashboard in charts/perf-canary-dashboard.json.
